slides.0.title: Five Major Wine Region Groups
slides.0.subtitle: From Tokaj's Sweet Wines to Villány's Red Wines
slides.1.title: Tokaj Region: Geographic Location
slides.1.componentProps.description: Tokaj sits in the north-eastern corner of Hungary, at the confluence of the Bodrog and Tisza rivers, at the foot of the Zemplén Mountains. The distinctive river-valley topography creates the perfect conditions for autumn noble rot development.
slides.2.title: Tokaj Region — King of the World's Sweet Wines
slides.2.highlights.0.title: UNESCO World Heritage Site
slides.2.highlights.0.content: The Tokaj Wine Region Historic Cultural Landscape was inscribed on the UNESCO World Cultural Heritage List in 2002 — the crown jewel of Hungarian wine
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Scale
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Approximately 5,723 hectares spanning 27 villages; First Class Vineyards are concentrated on the south-facing slopes of the volcanic hills
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Sweet Wine Legend
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Tokaji Aszú is the world's first documented botrytis sweet wine — roughly 100 years before France's Sauternes
slides.2.highlights.3.title: 21st-Century Dry Wine Revolution
slides.2.highlights.3.content: Since the 21st century, premium dry Furmint has become Tokaj's new calling card, standing shoulder to shoulder with the famous sweet wines
slides.2.content:
Tokaj occupies the north-eastern corner of Hungary, at the confluence of the Bodrog and Tisza rivers — a location unlike any other in the wine world.

🗺️ Geographic Facts

  • Location: North-eastern Hungary, beneath the Zemplén Mountains
  • Elevation: 130–400 m above sea level
  • Soils: Rhyolite tuff, loess and clay
  • Rivers: Bodrog + Tisza (source of autumn fog)

🍷 Main Wine Styles

Tokaji Aszú (3–6 Puttonyos) — The flagship botrytis sweet wine, honeyed and complex
Eszencia (450–800 g/L sugar) — Pure botrytised berry essence; extraordinarily rare
Szamorodni (dry or sweet) — Whole-cluster harvest; dry style resembles Sherry
Dry Furmint — The modern dry white revolution; mineral-driven and age-worthy

🏰 Famous Estates

Royal Tokaji · Béres Szőlőbirtok · Oremus (Vega Sicilia) · Disznókő (AXA Millésimes) · Tokaj Erzsébet Pince
slides.3.title: Eger Region: Geographic Location
slides.3.componentProps.description: Eger lies at the foot of the Bükk Mountains in northern Hungary. Its rhyolite tuff hills give Egri Bikavér (Bull's Blood) its distinctive minerality.
slides.4.title: Upper Hungary — Eger, Mátra, Bükk
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Birthplace of Bull's Blood
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Eger is the home of Egri Bikavér (Bull's Blood), the heart of northern Hungarian wine culture
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Volcanic Hill Topography
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Rhyolite tuff hills, with north-eastern mountain ranges blocking cold winds; the microclimate is warm with ample sunshine
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Diverse Varieties
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Reds led by Kékfrankos, Kadarka and Merlot; whites led by Olaszrizling and Chardonnay
slides.4.highlights.3.title: Mátra: Hungary's Largest PDO
slides.4.highlights.3.content: Mátraalja is Hungary's largest single wine region by area, renowned for approachable, good-value white wines
slides.4.content:
The Upper Hungary cluster comprises three adjacent regions — Eger, Mátra and Bükk — each with its own character, united by volcanic geology and a cooler northern climate.

🐂 Eger

Hungary's most important quality red wine region in the north. Egri Bikavér must use at least 3 varieties with Kékfrankos dominant; a Superior certification sets even stricter standards. Excellent whites too, especially Egri Leányka.

🌾 Mátra

Hungary's largest wine region by area. Known for approachable, affordable white wines and Muscat varieties — the everyday wine backbone of the north.

❄️ Bükk

The smallest and coolest of the three northern regions. Produces crisp, high-acid white wines and is especially valued for its preservation of native varieties.
slides.5.title: Villány Region: Geographic Location
slides.5.componentProps.description: Villány lies at the southernmost tip of Hungary, with an average annual temperature of 11.6°C — the highest in the country. Its limestone and red clay soils nurture Hungary's greatest red wines.
slides.6.title: Pannon Region — Hungary's Red Wine Capital
slides.6.highlights.0.title: Warmest Regional Group
slides.6.highlights.0.content: Villány's average annual temperature of 11.6°C makes it Hungary's warmest wine region — Bordeaux varieties achieve full ripeness here
slides.6.highlights.1.title: Cradle of Top Red Wines
slides.6.highlights.1.content: Villány and Szekszárd are Hungary's universally acclaimed premium red wine regions, earning international scores that rival southern France
slides.6.highlights.2.title: Villány
slides.6.highlights.2.content: Famous above all for Cabernet Franc; the "Villányi Franc" certified brand has become Hungary's most prestigious red wine designation
slides.6.highlights.3.title: Szekszárd
slides.6.highlights.3.content: Another Bikavér heartland, celebrated for the finest Kadarka preservation and rich, powerful Kékfrankos
slides.6.content:
The Pannon region is Hungary's red wine heartland — warmer, sunnier and more Mediterranean in character than anywhere else in the country.

☀️ Villány

  • Avg. temperature: 11.6°C (Hungary's highest)
  • Soils: Limestone + red clay
  • Varieties: Cab. Franc / Merlot / Cab. Sauv.
  • Flagship: Villányi Franc (certified brand)
  • Estates: Bock · Gere · Malatinszky · Vylyan

🌾 Szekszárd

  • Soils: Loess hills
  • Varieties: Kékfrankos / Kadarka / Cab. Franc
  • Wines: Szekszárdi Bikavér · rich Kékfrankos
  • Estates: Dúzsi · Heimann · Sebestyén
slides.7.title: Balaton and Duna Regions
slides.7.highlights.0.title: Lake Balaton
slides.7.highlights.0.content: Central Europe's largest freshwater lake; the water mass moderates temperatures, and Badacsony's basalt volcanic soil is the cradle of unique white wines
slides.7.highlights.1.title: Badacsony Volcano
slides.7.highlights.1.content: The basalt volcanic hills on Lake Balaton's northern shore produce Olaszrizling and Szürkebarát with an unmatched mineral intensity
slides.7.highlights.2.title: Duna Plain
slides.7.highlights.2.content: Kunság, Hajós-Baja and Csongrád are dominated by vast sandy plains, producing large volumes of accessible, everyday table wine
slides.7.highlights.3.title: Historical Significance of Sandy Soils
slides.7.highlights.3.content: The sandy soils of the Duna plain protected most vines from the phylloxera crisis of the 19th century
slides.7.content:
The Balaton and Duna regions represent two very different faces of Hungarian wine: volcanic artisan whites around the lake, and high-volume everyday wines across the plains.

🌊 Balaton Region (5 Sub-Regions)

Badacsony — Basalt volcanic; powerful minerality; finest Olaszrizling and Szürkebarát
Balatonfüred-Csopak — Limestone; crisp high acidity; refined white wines
Balatonboglár — South shore; warmer; Bordeaux varieties
Balatonfelvidék — Volcanic; high altitude; cool and fresh style
Somló — Independent volcanic hill; rare Juhfark

🌾 Duna Plain (3 Regions)

Kunság · Hajós-Baja · Csongrád — Hungary's largest growing area by volume; sandy plains; everyday wines

slides.8.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge Check
Tokaji Aszú is the world's first recorded botrytis sweet wine — approximately how many years before France's Sauternes was it first documented?
A. About 50 years
B. About 200 years
C. About 100 years
D. About 30 years

The earliest written records of Tokaji Aszú date to the 1630s, while Château d'Yquem in Sauternes produced its first documented botrytised wine around 1847. This places Tokaj approximately 100–200 years ahead. Louis XIV's famous declaration "Wine of Kings, King of Wines" further cemented its legendary status.
What are the production rules for Egri Bikavér (Eger Bull's Blood)?
A. Must be made from a single grape variety only
B. Must use at least 3 grape varieties, with Kékfrankos as the dominant variety
C. Must be 100% Kadarka
D. No variety restrictions — any Eger-grown red qualifies

Egri Bikavér regulations require a minimum of 3 grape varieties in the blend, with Kékfrankos constituting the largest single share. A higher-tier "Bikavér Superior" certification also exists, requiring stricter selection criteria and longer ageing.
Why is Villány considered the best Hungarian region for Bordeaux-variety red wines?
A. Because Villány is the oldest wine region in Hungary
B. Because Villány has the largest vineyard area in Hungary

C. Because Villány is Hungary's southernmost and warmest region, with an average of 11.6°C, Mediterranean influence, and limestone-plus-red-clay soils that allow Cabernet Franc and Merlot to reach full ripeness
D. Because Villány uses the most advanced winemaking technology

Villány's combination of Hungary's highest average temperature (11.6°C), Mediterranean climatic influence from the south, and limestone-rich red clay soils allows international Bordeaux varieties — especially Cabernet Franc — to ripen fully and achieve the depth and structure needed for world-class red wines.
Why does Badacsony Olaszrizling display far greater minerality than the same variety grown in other regions?
A. Badacsony winemakers use special fermentation techniques
B. Badacsony has a much cooler climate
C. Badacsony's basalt volcanic soil has strong heat retention and the volcanic minerals are absorbed by the vines
D. Badacsony uses older vine stock than other regions

Badacsony's black basalt volcanic rock is unique in Lake Balaton's wine landscape. It absorbs solar heat by day and radiates it at night, while the volcanic minerals are taken up by the vine roots and expressed in the wine. This is why Badacsony Olaszrizling has a mineral intensity and complexity that is simply unmatched elsewhere.
